unit.why: A short folktale quoted from Sefer ha-Hinukh: a dying sage tells his son to test his hundred friends, and none passes the test. It is followed by sages' maxims on friendship and keeping secrets.
unit.boundary_note: the trailing heading 'מענין אורח' introduces the next division's topic (hospitality) and belongs to it

stories.start_quote: חכם אחד צוה את בנו לפני מותו
stories.summary_en: A dying sage asks his son how many friends he has made; the son says a hundred, the father says he made only half a friend in his whole life, the son tests his friends and finds not one true, and the tale closes with maxims on friends and secrets.

tags.why: The text is an exemplary tale plus maxims, framed as moral instruction on choosing and testing friends.

quotes: אל תאהב ואל תהלל האוהב טרם שתנסהו ותבחנהו
tags.why: The tale's point is the virtue of prudence in friendship.
The son realizes too late that his many friends were not true friends.
